standard: Rendered information must be relevant to the current user, context, data, capability state and reporting period.
release_rule: Fabricated, stale, generic, unreachable or contextually misleading rendering is a product correctness defect.

confirmed_findings.finding: Seven-bar trend is hard-coded and does not represent persisted historical business data.
Progress bar is hard-coded to 70% without a verified goal denominator.
Rendered representations can imply analytical context that is not fully backed by corresponding historical/goal datasets.

Transactions, deals and staff queries rely on RLS rather than explicitly scoping the rendered dataset by business_id, while failures are converted to null and then rendered as absence. This makes tenant relevance and load-failure semantics dependent on hidden policy behavior.

The card is titled Cash & Receivables but prefers an overdue/receivable metric and labels the dominant value Outstanding receivables. It can therefore communicate cash position when the underlying fact is only receivables.

Intelligence loads are intentionally best-effort and failures are swallowed. Cards can render their generic degraded/empty presentation without exposing which capability failed, which can make an unavailable intelligence source look like a legitimate absence of business signal.

Report queries have no reporting-period selector, and query failures are caught without an error state; the initial zero-valued stats can therefore be rendered as real zero business results. The page also presents aggregate counts without an explicit period.

Income, expenses and net flow are calculated over every loaded cashflow record with no explicit period/filter, while the surface is presented as current Cash Flow. Query failures are logged but not represented to the user.

TargetsTab and CommissionsTab load in useEffect with empty dependency arrays even though businessId/staffId arrive from auth context. If the component mounts before auth resolves, it can permanently render an empty state for the wrong/no context.

Progress is calculated directly from actual_revenue/revenue_target without guarding a missing or zero denominator, so NaN/Infinity can reach the UI and the target progress is not explicitly tied to the selected reporting date beyond the stored target status.

MONTHS builds local dates and converts them through toISOString().slice(0,10). In positive-offset locales this can shift period_start/period_end to the previous UTC date, so the displayed month can query the wrong boundaries.

The page labels the narrative as FACT-level while composeBusinessReview is loaded independently and best-effort after the monthly_review payload. The narrative can therefore have different availability/timing semantics from the authoritative review payload and should not be presented as equally certified without shared evidence metadata.

The hub always renders a Market Benchmarks panel with a default metric of salary_software_engineer_ng, regardless of the current user's role, industry, selected tools or stated need. This is generic content rather than demonstrated user-relevant intelligence.
All intelligence RPC failures become data=null and render 'No data available.' That conflates an RPC failure/unavailable capability with a legitimate zero/empty intelligence result.
The product needs explicit distinctions between zero, empty, unknown, loading, error, unauthorized, not configured and not connected.

required_checks: Every displayed number traces to authoritative current data.
Every chart traces to real data points.
Every percentage has a defined numerator and denominator.
Every date/time label matches its actual reporting period.
Every rendered action performs the promised operation.
Role, entitlement and selected-tool context control what is rendered.
Tenant boundaries are preserved in displayed data.
Unavailable capabilities do not render as operational.
Mobile rendering preserves business meaning and critical actions.
No illustrative data is presented as live business data.
No fixed progress, trend or health score is presented without an authoritative source.
Visible counts agree with the underlying filtered dataset.
Visible labels describe the actual entity, status and time period being shown.
Filters and tabs change the evidence shown, not just the visual chrome.
Auth-dependent queries re-run when the authenticated business/user context becomes available.
Best-effort intelligence failures are visible as unavailable/error rather than indistinguishable from empty data.
Composite cards name the exact fact being shown rather than a broader business concept.
Default benchmark/insight panels are contextually relevant or explicitly user-selected.
